description: A CLI for creating better commits following the conventional commits specification

summary.one_liner: A TypeScript CLI that walks you through writing Conventional Commits messages via interactive prompts, and includes a companion tool, better-branch, for consistent branch and worktree naming.
summary.what_it_does: better-commits builds a conventional commit message through a series of prompts for type, scope, ticket, title, body, and footers, then previews it before running git commit. It infers ticket, commit type, and scope from the current branch name to pre-fill those fields. Behavior is configured through a .better-commits.jsonc file, either globally in the home directory or per repository via better-commits-init. The better-branch command creates branches or git worktrees using the same type and scope lists, with optional pre- and post-checkout shell hooks. A --no-interactive mode with CLI flags supports scripting and AI coding agents, and --dry-run validates the git command without committing.
use_cases: generate consistent commit messages from a script or AI coding agent
infer ticket and scope from branch names
create branches or git worktrees with standardized names
auto-populate pull request titles from first commit
enforce commit type and scope lists across a team repo
notable: Infers ticket, scope, and commit type from branch names
better-branch creates worktrees as a single folder while keeping the full branch name
Pre/post hooks for branch and worktree creation with template variables like {{TICKET}}
--no-interactive and --dry-run flags designed for scripts and coding agents
Optional trailers per commit type for changelog automation
caveats: Git Bash on Windows can fail with a TTY initialization error; alternatives suggested in README
Multi-line commit input on Windows may need a shell override in config
